newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: WAGES FIGURES IN ENTERPRISE BARGAINING

The Federal Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, says the latest figures on wages in enterprise bargaining show outcomes have effectively remained unchanged at under five per cent for the last nine months.
He says the figures show the average annual wage increase for federal wage agreements formalised in the March quarter was up point three per cent to four-point-seven per cent.
In the private sector, the average annual increase was 4.8 percent, up 0.4 per cent.
The average yearly increase for all Federal and private sector agreements at the end of March was just under five per cent.
COSTELLO SAYS DEAL CLAIMS RUBBISH
Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has described as "rubbish" retiring News Limited Chief Ken Cowley's claim of a Government deal with rival Kerry Packer over media ownership.
Mr Cowley says he's concerned some ministers have made commitments which include leaving foreign ownership limits in place.
But the Treasurer's told Radio 6-P-R in Perth, it's absolute rubbish, and Mr Cowley is merely arguing the News Limited case.
Mr Costello says with 60 percent of the newspapers in Australia, News Limited is not disinterested in media policy in this country.
COSTELLO SAYS HE DOESN'T SAVE ENOUGH
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, who has indicated he'll claim the Government's savings rebate, says he's unapologetic about it, because he doesn't save enough and should do more.
The Prime Minister has said he won't be claiming the rebate of up to 450 dollars, and Opposition leader Kim Beazley says he'll give his to charity.
Mr Costello says the Government wants more people to save, and he wants everyone to get the rebate.
FAMILY UNIFICATION PROGRAM TO BE HIT BY IMMIGRATION CUTS
The Immigration Minister says planned cuts to Australia's immigration intake will affect the program which reunites families.
Phillip Ruddock says there'll also be a greater focus on skilled migrants.
The Federal Government announced the cuts today saying they're necessary because of Australia's high level of unemployment.
The immigration intake will be reduced by about 20 per cent on the figures of the past two years, taking the number of immigrants to 68-thousand.
A further 12-thousand will be permitted to enter on humanitarian grounds.
It's the second time the Howard government has reduced Australia's immigration intake.
MOORE SAYS GOVT WILL RESPOND TO TAX REFORM DEBATE
The Federal Industry Minister, John Moore, says the Federal Government will give a response on the tax reform issue.
Mr Moore says the tax reform debate of the past few days will become an issue at the next election, but he's declined to say what type of reform the government is considering.
HILTON BOMBER LOSES APPEAL

The self-confessed Hilton Hotel bomber has today lost an appeal against his conviction in New South Wales' highest court. Evan Dunstan Pederick is serving a maximum 20-year prison sentence after being found guilty of murder and conspiracy to murder following the fatal bombing in 1978.
Three people died when a bomb exploded in a rubbish bin outside the Sydney Hilton Hotel.
Pederick admitted to police 11 years later that he built a bomb and planted it near the Hilton Hotel.
He was found guilty of three counts of murder and one of conspiring to murder the Indian Prime Minister who was attending a Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting.
Today the New South Wales Court of Criminal Appeal ruled that Pederick had given no evidence about a false confession.
BHP WORKERS ON STRIKE AT WHYALLA STEELWORKS
About 15-hundred workers have gone on strike for 24-hours at BHP's Whyalla steelworks.
More than 500 union members met this morning.
Workers at most other BHP steel sites went on strike last week.
The ACTU has called for strike action in protest against the company's decision to end steelmaking at Newcastle.
Australian Workers Union Organiser, Jeff Buckland, says workers are worried about the future of the steel industry.
PROCEEDINGS ADJOURNED IN JANA/SEVEN CASE
Proceedings in the case between Channel Seven and Jana Wendt in the New South Wales Industrial Commission have been adjourned for the day to allow discussion between the two parties.
Ms Wendt's barrister, John West QC, made the application this morning after extensive talks which delayed the commencement of proceedings.
Counsel for Seven, Steven Rothman, told the court the parties would be discussing issues which will take some period of time to resolve.
Justice Frank Marks welcomed the request and said he was assured it will be time well spent.
He's also refused an application by media organisations to lift restrictions on parts of evidence which were banned from reporting yesterday.
